metadata.note: The Elmira - Cortland - Canastota - Camden corridor in central New York before the Lehigh Valley ran it: the Cazenovia & Canastota (1870-1878), the Cazenovia, Canastota & DeRuyter (1878-1884), the Utica, Ithaca & Elmira (1872-1884, including two trackage-rights legs drawn on other roads' alignments), and the Elmira, Cortland & Northern (1884-1896, with the 1887 Camden Extension). The Lehigh Valley bought the EC&N on Feb 20 1896 and operated it from that day; the LV-era pieces (1896-1950) are in lehigh_valley_railroad.geojson, split by passenger end: Elmira - East Ithaca 1896-1935, East Ithaca - Cortland 1896-1950, Cortland - Canastota 1896-1950 [OPEN], Canastota - Camden 1896-1935. Each company has its own colour and each operator era is its own feature sharing geometry (Rule 4). Research report: research/branches/elmira_cortland_and_northern_railroad.txt.

Cazenovia & Canastota opening: Dec 7 1870 (MAR, Cazenovia Republican via marker) vs Dec 7 1869 (Wikipedia). Drawn from 1870.

All headway_min values are estimates; MAR gives train counts for a few dates (1870, 1887, 1900, 1928, 1949) but no headways were read.

The report's '~27 mi via Candor, Willseyville' for the UI&E's 1873-1875 Ithaca & Athens trackage is contradicted by the I&A's own route (Spencer - West Danby - Ithaca, traced 20.4 mi); Candor and Willseyville are on the DL&W.

segments.note: Cazenovia & Canastota Railroad: chartered April 1868, built from April 1869 and completed December 7 1870, when three trains each way Mon-Sat began running Cazenovia - Canastota (MAR ch.3); the Cazenovia Republican of Dec 7 1870 announced the regular trips (historical marker). CONFLICT: Wikipedia gives Dec 7 1869 - same day, one year earlier; the drawn start uses the later year of the bracket. Steam from the first train, so no animal-power years. Ends 1878, when the C&C merged with the Cazenovia & DeRuyter (built 1877-78) to form the Cazenovia, Canastota & DeRuyter - see that feature. headway_min is an ESTIMATE derived from MAR's count of three round trips a day, not a timetable with times.

segments.note: Cazenovia, Canastota & DeRuyter Railroad: formed 1878 by merging the Cazenovia & Canastota with the Cazenovia & DeRuyter, whose 13.9-mile Cazenovia - DeRuyter extension opened for service in November 1878 (MAR ch.3, ch.14). British-investor control (1878), the May 1882 receivership (receiver G. J. Rice) and Austin Corbin's 1882 purchase were stock changes under the same operating company, not operator changes. By 1882 a joint UI&E-CC&D timetable advertised through Elmira - East Ithaca - Cortland - Cazenovia - Canastota service (MAR ch.3; MAR's caption dates the reproduced joint timetable '1872', which cannot be right). Trackage rights over the NY&OM DeRuyter - Cortland were secured in 1878, but whether CC&D trains themselves ran over them is not established, so DeRuyter - Cortland is not drawn under this company (see the UI&E Cortland - DeRuyter feature). Ends Mar 7 1884, when the CC&D's assets passed to the new Elmira, Cortland & Northern. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a timetable reading.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 19.8 mi against 19.4 mi documented (MAR MP 50.7-70.1). East Ithaca - Cortland 19.8 mi via Varna, Etna, Freeville and McLean on the Dryden Rail Trail / E&C grade (MAR 50.7-70.1 = 19.4 mi). No straight-line legs. The western end is the later East Ithaca (Maple Ave) station site; the 1871-1876 extension to the Cornell campus terminus (junction near MP 51.4) is NOT drawn because its geometry was not identified, so 1872-1876 is drawn about a mile short of that era's terminus.

segments.note: Built by the Ithaca & Cortland Railroad: Freeville - a point east of Ithaca completed May 1871, extended to a terminus on the Cornell University campus late 1871, and merged into the Utica, Ithaca & Elmira in October 1871; Freeville - Cortland completed February 1872 (MAR ch.3). Drawn from 1872, the first year both ends were open and the UI&E certainly the operating company - no I&C-operated passenger train is confirmed for May-Oct 1871, so that company is not drawn. From March 1872 New York & Oswego Midland trains also used Cortland - Freeville under a trackage exchange (MAR ch.3). From April 1875 to May 1876 the UI&E also ran the bankrupt NY&OM's Norwich - Cortland and Freeville - Scipio Center services (not drawn here). Through Elmira service via Brookton began Dec 11 1875; the campus service was dropped and its track removed in 1876. Fowler's letter y (1875 Official Guide) lists Ithaca (ECN), Freeville and Cortland. The 1878 foreclosure to British investors, the May 1882 receivership and Corbin's 1882 purchase did not change the operating company. Ends Mar 7 1884 at the EC&N's formation. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a timetable reading.
sources: Segment-level: dates from MAR ch.3 (I&C construction 1871, merger Oct 1871, Freeville - Cortland Feb 1872) and ch.4 (EC&N Mar 7 1884) (dates as extracted from MAR by research/branches/elmira_cortland_and_northern_railroad.txt; the tracer did not re-read MAR); Fowler letter y corroborates 1875 service. Ends with the Dec 11 1875 opening of the UI&E's own line via Brookton; 1875 is also drawn on that feature. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a timetable reading.

Ends Mar 7 1884 at the EC&N's formation. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a timetable reading.

segments.note: TRACKAGE RIGHTS over New York & Oswego Midland (NY&OM, from 1879/80 NYO&W) track built 1872, drawn in the UI&E's colour on the other road's track. The UI&E held rights from March 1872 and the CC&D 'secured' rights in 1878 (MAR ch.3); MAR ch.15 speaks of trains running Elmira - East Ithaca - Freeville - Cortland - DeRuyter 'in 1875', and Fowler's letter y (1875 Guide) lists DeRuyter, Cuyler and Truxton - but those could be the NY&OM's own Norwich - Cortland trains, which used this track until the NY&OM abandoned Norwich - DeRuyter in 1882 (MAR ch.8). The first firm evidence of UI&E/CC&D through service is the 1882 joint timetable. START IS THE EARLIEST CONFIRMED YEAR, NOT A KNOWN OPENING: through trains may have run any time from 1872; do not move the start earlier without a timetable. Which of the UI&E or CC&D ran the trains is also not established; drawn under the UI&E per the report. Ends Mar 7 1884, when the EC&N assumed the NYO&W lease. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a timetable reading.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 117.6 mi against 118.5 mi documented (MAR MP 0.5-119.0; '120 miles of main track' in 1883). Built from: Elmira - Horseheads 4.4 mi on the OSM 'Elmira and Cortland branch' grade, i.e. the Canal Railroad alignment of 1881 (MAR 0.5-5.6 = 5.1 mi; the drawn line starts at the south end of the mapped grade at about Elmira's Fifth St, which is MAR's MP 0.5 station area, and Horseheads is pinned on the grade at the village, so the 0.7 mi shortfall is the waypoint, not the route); Horseheads - Van Etten 19.5 mi on the E&C grade via Breesport, Erin, Park Station and Swartwood (MAR 5.6-25.2 = 19.6 mi; AR 24.7 mi Elmira - Van Etten); Van Etten - Spencer - East Ithaca 25.3 mi (MAR 25.2-50.7 = 25.5 mi): the branch's OWN Van Etten - Spencer track (built early 1876), then the E&C grade via West Candor, Willseyville, Brooktondale and Besemer to the East Ithaca (Maple Ave) station site; about 1.1 mi near Besemer-East Ithaca is on untagged OpenHistoricalMap railway ways that follow the same grade; East Ithaca - Cortland 19.8 mi via Varna, Etna, Freeville and McLean on the Dryden Rail Trail / E&C grade (MAR 50.7-70.1 = 19.4 mi); Cortland - DeRuyter 19.9 mi via East Homer, Truxton and Cuyler on the OSM E&C grade, which is the NY&OM-built track of 1872 (MAR ch.14 gives 18.6 mi; MAR mileposts 70.1-90.4 give 20.3); DeRuyter - Cazenovia 13.9 mi via Sheds Corners and New Woodstock (MAR 13.9 mi); Cazenovia - Canastota 14.7 mi via Chittenango Falls and Perryville (MAR 104.3-119.0 = 14.7 mi), ending at the E&C's Canastota station by the NYC main line. No straight-line legs. Per-station mileposts on the drawn Elmira - Canastota line vs MAR's station list: Elmira 0.5 (0.5), Horseheads 4.9 (5.6), Van Etten 24.4 (25.2), Spencer 27.7 (27.7), East Ithaca 49.8 (50.7), Freeville 58.9 (59.7), Cortland 69.6 (70.1), DeRuyter 89.5 (90.4), Cazenovia 103.4 (104.3), Canastota 118.1 (119.0). Despike was left on; the East Ithaca horseshoe (line runs north into the station and leaves north-east) lies on a join between separately traced pieces, so it is drawn whole.

segments.note: Elmira, Cortland & Northern Railroad, incorporated Mar 7 1884 under the NY General Railroad Act, took over the assets of the Utica, Ithaca & Elmira and the Cazenovia, Canastota & DeRuyter and assumed the leases of the Canal Railroad (Elmira - Horseheads) and of the NYO&W's Cortland - DeRuyter track (MAR ch.4) - the same trains as the UI&E/CC&D joint service before it. Austin Corbin president, A. A. McLeod general manager. 1883: about 170,000 passengers on the predecessors; 1889: about 261,802 on the EC&N (MAR ch.3-4). First-class passenger trains ran alongside mixed 'accommodation' trains; an 1894 summer timetable is reproduced in MAR. Ends Feb 20 1896, when the Lehigh Valley bought the EC&N and began operating it as its Elmira and Cortland Branch (MAR ch.6) - the Rule 4 split date. The EC&N lingered as a paper company until the 1905 merger, which changed nothing about who ran the trains. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a timetable reading.

properties.geometry_quality: Canastota - Camden 20.4 mi against MAR's 20.7 mi (MP 119.0-139.7). Built from: a 0.35 mi STRAIGHT LINE at Canastota from the E&C station by the NYC main line east to the start of the mapped Camden-extension grade (the 1887 connection through the station area is not mapped; the route was found only as abandoned/disused NYC-tagged sidings); about 1.2 mi (before simplification) of NYC-tagged disused/abandoned sidings, untagged rail and short graph connectors around that junction; 17.2 mi of the OSM 'Elmira and Cortland Branch' grade via South Bay, Sylvan Junction, Vienna and McConnellsville; and the last 2.5 mi into Camden on the abandoned RW&O 'Rome Branch' (NYC-tagged) alignment, which the E&C grade joins at about 43.302 N, 75.718 W. Whether the EC&N/LV had its own track beside the RW&O into Camden or used RW&O track is NOT established; this leg is drawn on the RW&O's alignment and should be read as approximate. The Sylvan Beach wye is not drawn.

segments.note: The Camden Extension, built 1886-87 by the Canastota Northern Railroad and leased to the EC&N for $18,000 a year - the Canastota Northern never ran its own trains, so there is no separate operator. Construction was completed and 'regular service inaugurated in July 1887', with 'one or two passenger and one freight-accommodation train in each direction daily except Sundays', plus summer excursions to Sylvan Beach on a wye; interchange with the RW&O at Camden (MAR ch.4). Ends Feb 20 1896 when the Lehigh Valley took over operation (MAR ch.6). headway_min is an ESTIMATE from MAR's train count, not a timetable with times.
